data.name: ClaudeSessionsSource
data.value: Claude Code sessions
data.comment: A sensor source, as in "Claude Code sessions is unavailable: …".

data.name: ClaudeLimitsSource
data.value: Claude Code limits
data.comment: A sensor source.

data.name: CodexLimitsSource
data.value: Codex limits
data.comment: A sensor source.

data.name: CodexSessionsSource
data.value: Codex sessions
data.comment: A sensor source.

data.name: SourceUnavailable
data.value: {0} is unavailable: {1}
data.comment: {0} is a sensor source, {1} the reason.

data.name: FpsNeedsAdministrator
data.value: FPS is off: PresentMon needs Marquee to run as administrator. Set `providers: { fps: off }` in config.yaml to stop this message.
data.comment: Logged at start when the FPS provider is on but Marquee isn't elevated. PresentMon is a program's name; `providers: { fps: off }` and config.yaml stay as they are.

data.name: NoTheme
data.value: No theme to show. Pass a theme folder to `marquee run`, or set theme: in config.yaml.
data.comment: Neither the command line nor config.yaml names a theme. "theme:" is the config.yaml key and stays as it is.

data.name: ThemeFolderNotFound
data.value: There is no theme folder at {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the full path that was given.

data.name: ThemeNotFound
data.value: Theme '{0}' was not found. Marquee looked for a folder of that name in: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the theme's name as given, {1} the folders searched, separated by semicolons.

data.name: ConfigUnreadable
data.value: Could not read {0} ({1}); using the default settings.
data.comment: {0} is the path of config.yaml, {1} the reason.

data.name: ConfigInvalidUsingDefaults
data.value: {0} (Marquee uses the default settings until the file is fixed)
data.comment: {0} is the error in config.yaml, starting with its line number.

data.name: CouldNotReadConfig
data.value: Could not read config.yaml: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason.

data.name: CouldNotApplyConfig
data.value: Could not apply config.yaml: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason.

data.name: NoScreenFound
data.value: No supported screen found. Run `marquee devices` to check.

data.name: ShowingTheme
data.value: Showing theme '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the theme's name.

data.name: LastGoodLayoutStays
data.value: {0} (the last good layout stays on screen until the file is fixed)
data.comment: {0} is the error in the theme's layout.

data.name: SettingsChanged
data.value: The settings changed; applying the new ones.

data.name: PreviousSettingsKept
data.value: The new settings could not be applied, so Marquee kept the previous ones.
data.comment: Follows the reason the new settings failed, such as a theme error or no screen.

data.name: WaitingForTheme
data.value: Once theme '{0}' is fixed and saved, Marquee switches to it with the new settings.
data.comment: Follows PreviousSettingsKept when the new settings name a theme that didn't load. {0} is the theme's name.

data.name: ThemeStillFails
data.value: {0} (Marquee switches to this theme once it loads)
data.comment: {0} is the error in a theme that new settings are waiting for (see WaitingForTheme), after it was saved again.

data.name: SavingLimitsFailed
data.value: Saving the Claude Code limits failed: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason.

data.name: StartFailed
data.value: Marquee could not start: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, an unexpected error.

data.name: SettingsChangeFailed
data.value: Applying the new settings failed ({0}), so Marquee stopped. It starts again at the next settings change.
data.comment: {0} is the reason, an unexpected error part-way through a config.yaml change.

data.name: HandlerFailed
data.value: A handler of the engine's events failed: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason. A handler is code in the tray or `marquee run` that reacts to a theme loading or failing.

data.name: LogonTaskDescription
data.value: Starts Marquee's tray app when you log on, with administrator rights where your account has them, so it can read game FPS and take the screen over from L-Connect. Installed and removed with Marquee.
data.comment: The logon task's description, shown in Task Scheduler's window. "Marquee" and "L-Connect" are names.

data.name: SchTasksFailed
data.value: schtasks exited with code {0}: {1}
data.comment: {0} is schtasks.exe's exit code, {1} what it printed (Windows' own text, already in the user's language). "schtasks" is a program's name.

data.name: TaskFileChanged
data.value: The logon task's file {0} changed after Marquee wrote it, so the task was not installed. Something else is writing in that folder: install Marquee into Program Files.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the XML file Marquee writes for Task Scheduler. "Program Files" is Windows' folder: use its name in the user's language.

data.name: SchTasksTimedOut
data.value: schtasks did not finish within {0} seconds and was stopped.
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds. "schtasks" is a program's name.

data.name: SchTasksDidNotStart
data.value: schtasks did not start.
data.comment: "schtasks" is a program's name.

data.name: TaskSchedulerFailed
data.value: Task Scheduler could not start the task: {0}
data.comment: {0} is Task Scheduler's reason (Windows' own text, already in the user's language).

data.name: UpdatesFolderIsLink
data.value: {0} or the folder above it is a junction or symbolic link, so the downloaded updates in it were not deleted.
data.comment: {0} is the folder of downloaded updates, %ProgramData%\Marquee\updates.

data.name: RingUnavailable
data.value: The LED ring is unavailable: {0} Retrying every {1} s.
data.comment: {0} is the reason, a sentence ending in a full stop; {1} is a number of seconds. The LED ring is the ring of lights around the screen.

data.name: RingNotFound
data.value: No LED ring was found; Marquee keeps looking for one.
data.comment: Logged once when no LED ring (the ring of lights around the screen) is plugged in, which is normal for a screen without one.

data.name: RingConnected
data.value: Connected to the LED ring.
data.comment: Follows RingUnavailable or RingNotFound once the ring works.

data.name: RingFrameFailed
data.value: Lighting the LED ring failed: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, an unexpected error while working out the ring's colors.

data.name: HandoverAuto
data.value: L-Connect's service has the screen; taking it over, as `lconnect.handover: auto` says.
data.comment: Logged when Marquee starts taking the screen from L-Connect by itself. "L-Connect" is a program's name; `lconnect.handover: auto` is a config.yaml setting and stays as it is.

data.name: HandoverRetry
data.value: Trying again to take the screen from L-Connect's service, as `lconnect.handover: auto` says.
data.comment: Logged when Marquee tries again by itself, minutes after taking the screen from L-Connect failed (1, 2, 5, then every 10). "L-Connect" is a program's name; `lconnect.handover: auto` is a config.yaml setting and stays as it is.

data.name: HandoverScreenOpen
data.value: Marquee has the screen already, so there's nothing to take from L-Connect.
data.comment: Logged when a "Take over" (from the tray menu or a notification clicked late) comes after Marquee already got the screen, so nothing is done. "L-Connect" is a program's name.

data.name: HandoverHeldBack
data.value: L-Connect's service has the screen again, but taking it failed less than {0} s ago, so Marquee waits until then to try again.
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds. Logged instead of taking the screen from L-Connect again straight after a failed try; Marquee tries again once the seconds are up. "L-Connect" is a program's name.

data.name: HandoverNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Marquee can't take the screen from L-Connect: stopping L-Connect's service needs Marquee to run as administrator. Set `lconnect: { handover: off }` in config.yaml to stop this message.
data.comment: Logged once when L-Connect holds the screen and `lconnect.handover` is ask or auto, but Marquee isn't elevated. "L-Connect" is a program's name; `lconnect: { handover: off }` and config.yaml stay as they are.

data.name: TakeOverNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Marquee can't take the screen from L-Connect: stopping L-Connect's service needs Marquee to run as administrator, as its logon task starts it.
data.comment: Logged when someone asks Marquee to take the screen (the tray's "Take over") but Marquee isn't elevated. "L-Connect" is a program's name.

data.name: HandoverFailed
data.value: Couldn't take the screen from L-Connect: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, an unexpected error. "L-Connect" is a program's name.

data.name: ReleaseNotJson
data.value: GitHub's answer isn't JSON Marquee can read: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the JSON reader's own description of the problem. "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: ReleaseUnreadable
data.value: GitHub's answer doesn't describe a release: it should have a tag, say whether it is a draft or a prerelease, and list its files.
data.comment: "GitHub" is a name. A release's tag is its version, such as v1.2.3.

data.name: ReleaseIsDraft
data.value: Release {0} is a draft.
data.comment: {0} is the release's tag, such as v1.2.3.

data.name: ReleaseIsPrerelease
data.value: Release {0} is a prerelease.
data.comment: {0} is the release's tag, such as v1.2.3.

data.name: ReleaseTagNotAVersion
data.value: Release tag '{0}' isn't a version Marquee installs, which is v and three numbers, such as v1.2.3.
data.comment: {0} is the release's tag as GitHub gave it.

data.name: ReleaseFileMissing
data.value: Release {0} has no file named {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the release's tag, such as v1.2.3; {1} a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.

data.name: ReleaseFileUnreadable
data.value: The release doesn't say how big {0} is.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.

data.name: ReleaseFileSize
data.value: The release says {0} is {1} bytes, and Marquee only downloads it at 1 to {2} bytes.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi; {1} and {2} are numbers of bytes.

data.name: ReleaseFileNotOnGitHub
data.value: The release doesn't serve {0} from github.com over https, so Marquee won't download it.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi. "github.com" and "https" stay as they are.

data.name: UpdateCheckSkippedDevelopmentKey
data.value: This build of Marquee carries the placeholder release key, which no release is signed with, so it doesn't look for updates.
data.comment: The signing key is what proves an update comes from Marquee's author; a development build has a placeholder whose private half was never kept.

data.name: UpdateCheckSkippedNoVersion
data.value: Marquee doesn't look for updates: its own version, '{0}', isn't one it can compare.
data.comment: {0} is the version Marquee was built with, as text.

data.name: UpdateCheckTimedOut
data.value: GitHub didn't answer the update check within {0} seconds. Marquee looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds. "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: UpdateCheckFailed
data.value: The update check failed ({0}). Marquee looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: {0} is the reason, such as Windows' own text for a network error.

data.name: UpdateCheckHttpError
data.value: GitHub answered the update check with HTTP {0} {1}. Marquee looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: {0} is an HTTP status code, {1} its English name from the server. "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: UpdateCheckRateLimited
data.value: GitHub turned the update check away: requests from this network without a GitHub account have reached their hourly limit. Marquee looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: "GitHub" is a name. Marquee makes one request a day; the limit counts every program on the network.

data.name: NoReleaseYet
data.value: No Marquee release has been published on GitHub yet.
data.comment: "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: UpdateCheckAnswerTooLarge
data.value: GitHub's answer to the update check was over {0} bytes, so Marquee didn't read it. It looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: {0} is a number of bytes. "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: UpdateCheckUnusableRelease
data.value: The latest release on GitHub isn't one Marquee can install: {0} Marquee looks again tomorrow.
data.comment: {0} is the reason, one of the Release messages above, ending with a full stop.

data.name: UpToDate
data.value: Marquee {0} is up to date.
data.comment: {0} is the running version, such as 1.2.3.

data.name: UpdateAvailable
data.value: Marquee {0} is available (this is {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the new version, {1} the running one, such as 1.2.3.

data.name: UpdateCheckTimeNotSaved
data.value: Couldn't save the time of the update check in {0} ({1}). Until Marquee restarts it still checks once a day.
data.comment: {0} is a file's path, {1} the reason.

data.name: UpdateRefusedDevelopmentKey
data.value: Marquee won't install updates: this build carries the placeholder release key, which no release is signed with.
data.comment: The signing key is what proves an update comes from Marquee's author; a development build has a placeholder whose private half was never kept.

data.name: UpdateSignatureMissing
data.value: The update's signature, {0}, isn't there, so Marquee won't install the update.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.sig.

data.name: UpdateSignatureTooLarge
data.value: {0} is over {1} bytes, which no signature is, so Marquee won't install the update.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.sig; {1} a number of bytes.

data.name: UpdateSignatureInvalid
data.value: {0} couldn't be verified: its signature doesn't match the key built into Marquee, so it may have been changed. Marquee won't install it.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.

data.name: UpdateWrongSize
data.value: {0} isn't the {1} bytes the release says it is, so Marquee won't install it.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi; {1} a number of bytes.

data.name: UpdateDownloadHttpError
data.value: Downloading {0} failed: GitHub answered HTTP {1}.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi; {1} an HTTP status code. "GitHub" is a name.

data.name: UpdateDownloadFailed
data.value: Downloading the update failed: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, such as Windows' own text for a network or disk error.

data.name: UpdateDownloadStalled
data.value: Downloading the update stopped: nothing arrived for {0} seconds.
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds.

data.name: UpdateVerified
data.value: Downloaded {0} and verified its signature.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, such as Marquee-1.2.3-x64.msi.

data.name: InstallerStarting
data.value: Starting the installer for Marquee {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the new version, such as 1.2.3.

data.name: InstallerDidNotStart
data.value: The installer could not be started: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, Windows' own text.
